title: A Cozy Space Exploration Game(or not)
author: rekansebangku
selftext:
Hello everyone,

I just made a cozy space exploration game (though it's hard to even call it a game). The main goal is just mindless exploration around a solar system. I have loved space since I was a kid, so I just wanted a way to comfortably cruise around and enjoy the view.

It is built with Three.js with Cursor, so you can play it directly in your browser. Mobile support is there but still needs a lot of adjustments, so playing on desktop is better if possible.

For the assets, the textures are mostly from NASA, the 3D meshes are generated, and the spaceship was made using Meshy.

Just wanted to share this here. I hope there are other space exploration fans who might enjoy the experience.

Thanks!

[Spaceploration on Itch](https://ryansetiawan.itch.io/spaceploration)

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body:
Pretty good, OP. 

  
I would ditch WASD controls and go with A/Z for thrust. 

Also unify the fast travel and boost functions to the shift-button modifier. Juggling three 'thrust' modes at once is a bit awkward. 

I believe there's a good bunch of material available about the Outer Wilds engine, you should go read up on what they did to make their solar system work.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback. I see your point about the keybinds, especially for the thrust modes. It gets pretty crowded. I will definitely look into the Outer Wilds tech breakdown for inspiration on the navigation side of things. Appreciate the advice!

comments.author: barkywoodson
comments.body: Haven’t played it, but looks like something I would like. One comment about how it comes across in the screen shots posted here. I really want to see more of the ship, but all the shots are the same angle same pitch as the others, are you able to rotate the camera at all, or a slow follow when you change heading? I’ll try it out, but that’s just the question I have drm the screenshots.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: Right now the camera is locked behind the ship, which is why the shots look a bit samey. I honestly did not think about adding a free camera until you mentioned it, but it is a great idea to make the journey feel more cinematic. I am going to see if I can implement a slow orbit or a smoother follow-cam for a future update. Thanks for the heads up!

replies.author: promptling
replies.body: The camera change would make a clean before & after test: does a slow orbit make the journey feel more cinematic without making navigation less comfortable? I’m building [Patchloop](https://patchloop.io/) for agentically built games in progress, with repeat test rounds and a room around each project. Spaceploration feels like a lovely fit for a small group that follows these changes over time.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: That is a fair point regarding the balance between cinematic feel and control comfort. It is definitely going to be a balancing act to make the camera movement feel smooth without being distracting while navigating. I will have to do some prototyping to see how it feels in practice. Thanks for the input!

comments.author: Jolva
comments.body: Nice Jupiter! How did you make it?

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body:
Thanks! Honestly Jupiter is simpler than it looks 😄

It's basically a big 3D ball with a real photo of Jupiter from NASA wrapped around it. 

Then a few touches sell the "space" feeling:

* One light source acts as the Sun, so one side is lit and the other fades into shadow.
* The day/night line is softened on purpose so the light wraps gently across the cloud tops instead of a hard edge. Gas giants don't have a crisp horizon.
* A soft glowing rim around it and a warm "bloom" glow give it that majestic, lit-from-within look.
* It slowly spins (Jupiter's real day is under 10 hours, so it turns noticeably).

That's really it. A real texture + good lighting + a little glow. The whole game runs in the browser, no fancy pre-rendering.

replies.author: Jolva
replies.body:
My game is set in the asteroid belt with very lax rules regarding how close Jupiter is to any asteroids 😆 I made a low poly model for mine with a texture but I might go with a stylized version of your approach instead. Nice work and cool game!

https://preview.redd.it/90dg7p8gmvdh1.png?width=1058&format=png&auto=webp&s=da4a236437c29f9f5de08a788c7f1a7afa8f3d5e

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: That low poly Jupiter looks awesome! I am honestly a fan of that style. It has such a unique identity, and the colors are really vibrant. Plus, the performance benefits of that approach are massive for web-based projects. Definitely keep that style. it looks great!

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body: I think this is a nice start to a concept that could become a good simulation game. I would turn it into a full game where you have try to land the shuttle on earth.

replies.author: rekansebangku
replies.body: I have definitely thought about adding a landing mechanic! It sounds like the perfect next step. To be honest, I am still figuring out the technical side of how to make that transition feel smooth and satisfying, but it is definitely on my radar for future updates.
